ft09_interpretation.from_current_frame: Both candidate versions parse frame.ascii to rebuild cells and actions. Their real executions occurred on successive observed frames. next_candidate_recommendation.single_primary_problem: Bounded correction of program validation failures before spending real actions.
next_candidate_recommendation.minimal_change: Permit one feedback repair on an actually observed zero-action source/evaluation/schema failure, within the existing total120s extra budget and450s game window. Feed exact failing code, sanitized traceback/contract errors and unchanged current facts; no new rule hint, object segmentation, memory, trigger policy or extra action quota. Count this as a shared single followup quota with actual-mismatch repair to prevent unbounded retries.
next_candidate_recommendation.why: The dedicated interface now delivers code. su15 fails for a concrete generated implementation bug before any rule claim can be tested; discarding a full program without feedback leaves that diagnostic unanswered.
next_candidate_recommendation.limitation: This change only tests whether actual code feedback improves executable quality. It does not repair ft09 incorrect spatial abstraction or prove net score gain. A separate future candidate could study hypothesis-discriminating actions/context preservation; mixing these now would confound the next result.
next_candidate_recommendation.stop_condition: If executable programs still propose wrong dynamics and do not improve same-cut progression, move focus to competing rule hypotheses/probes; do not keep spending GPU on interface names or merely returning code.

causal_limits: Single B-then-A selected-checkpoint run does not establish stable effect, natural-trigger behavior, full25 performance or hidden-score transfer.
This audit identifies actual implementation/rule errors and useful counterexample consumption, not their isolated causal contribution to score regression.
Generated code was locally reproduced only on public observation data; no manually fixed program is proposed as a game-specific solver.
